title.zh-CN: 一局游戏，是怎样一步步发生的？
title.en: How Does a Game Happen, One Move at a Time?

summary.zh-CN: 跟着小兔与小刺猬走完四轮，理解谁行动、木板怎样变化，以及何时结束。
summary.en: Follow Rabbit and Hedgehog through four rounds to understand turns, changing supplies, and the end of a game.

title.zh-CN: 看过一局以后，究竟看到了什么？
title.en: What Have You Actually Seen After Watching a Game?

summary.zh-CN: 从第一轮的位置与木板变化，分清可核对的事件、自己的感受和对原因的猜想。
summary.en: Use first-round changes to separate observable events, your own feelings, and possible explanations.

title.zh-CN: 这款游戏给谁，在什么时候玩？
title.en: Who Will Play This Game, and When?

summary.zh-CN: 情境、邀请和停止如何变成可调整的起点；不按年龄猜经验。
summary.en: Why must a first design name a setting as well as an audience?

title.zh-CN: 还没有规则时，先确定什么？
title.en: What Can You Decide Before You Have Rules?

summary.zh-CN: 用合作过河说明暂定简报怎样区分玩家处境、制作条件、体验方向和待检问题。
summary.en: Use the shared crossing to distinguish player context, practical conditions, intended experience, and open questions in a provisional brief.

title.zh-CN: 有了方向，怎样想出不止一种做法？
title.en: How Can One Direction Lead to Several Ideas?

summary.zh-CN: 从同一过河时刻想出几种行动，再按目标和需补的规则选一个可执行的候选。
summary.en: Generate several actions for one crossing moment, then compare their purpose and supporting rules before choosing a candidate.

title.zh-CN: “让动物过河”，要变成哪些动作？
title.en: What Actions Turn “Help the Animals Cross” into a Game?

summary.zh-CN: 把过河意图写成有条件、代价和后果的动作，并给出能直接运行的完整纸片基本版。
summary.en: Turn the crossing intention into actions with conditions, costs, and consequences, using a complete playable paper draft.

title.zh-CN: 一个动作结束以后，桌上应该变成什么样？
title.en: What Should the Table Look Like After an Action?

summary.zh-CN: 跟着一次动作检查资格、付款、移动、换人和结束，避免同一纸片局面产生不同结果。
summary.en: Follow an action through permission, payment, movement, turn changes, and ending checks.

title.zh-CN: 轮到我时，为什么要想一想？
title.en: Why Pause to Think on My Turn?

summary.zh-CN: 同一个回合里，前进和收集怎样改变以后；看懂后果与替别人作决定有什么不同。
summary.en: Follow how moving or collecting changes later possibilities, and distinguish understanding a consequence from having someone choose for you.

title.zh-CN: 早一点知道天气，我能改做什么？
title.en: What Can I Change If I Know the Weather Earlier?

summary.zh-CN: 同一张天气牌，早揭晓能否改变动作，要看还有什么能做；抽走牌也会改变下一次机会。
summary.en: Whether an earlier reveal changes an action depends on available responses; removing a card also changes the next draw.

title.zh-CN: 木板够了，为什么还是来不及？
title.en: Why Can We Have Enough Planks but Still Run Out of Time?

summary.zh-CN: 木板足够与行动来得及是两回事；共同的七件事还要分给各自有限的机会。
summary.en: Enough planks do not ensure enough turns; the team’s required actions must fit each animal’s own opportunities.

title.zh-CN: 多一条路，选择会怎样变？
title.en: How Does Another Route Change the Choice?

summary.zh-CN: 短路用更多木板换一次行动；连接、费用与能否同处都要由规则说明。
summary.en: A shorter route trades more planks for a turn; connections, costs, and sharing a place need explicit rules.

title.zh-CN: 轮到别人时，我在等什么？
title.en: What Am I Waiting For on Someone Else’s Turn?

summary.zh-CN: 先做成一件事会改变后来人的判断；同时选择仍需要明确的执行次序。
summary.en: Completed actions inform later choices, while simultaneous selection still needs a clear resolution order.

title.zh-CN: 木板从哪里来，又到哪里去？
title.en: Where Do Planks Come From, and Where Do They Go?

summary.zh-CN: 追踪木板的来源与使用，再看原料、加工能力和补给怎样改变准备。
summary.en: Follow plank acquisition and use, then examine how raw material, processing capacity, and supply rules change preparation.

title.zh-CN: 目标和结束，怎样把一局连起来？
title.en: How Do Goals and Endings Hold a Game Together?

summary.zh-CN: 把争取的结果、计分、停下的条件与最后一次行动接在一起。
summary.en: Connect desired results, scoring, stopping conditions, and the final action.

title.zh-CN: 两个好点子，放在一起还好吗？
title.en: Do Two Good Ideas Still Work Well Together?

summary.zh-CN: 共用锯台与取回标记放在一起，别人一次使用怎样替你省掉一次行动？
summary.en: Combine a shared sawing station with marker retrieval to see how another person’s use can save your turn.

title.zh-CN: 一起获胜，为什么还要商量？
title.en: Why Discuss a Plan When We Win Together?

summary.zh-CN: 区分共同目标、个人权限、交流条件；核算互换收集者、强制开局与共同成功后个人名次的拉扯。
summary.en: What must people still decide when they share a goal?

title.zh-CN: 怎样判断一个办法太强了？
title.en: How Can We Tell Whether an Option Is Too Strong?

summary.zh-CN: 分别比较动作、能力、先后与人数，找出明显浪费以及供应改变后的可行计划。
summary.en: Compare actions, abilities, order, and player count separately to find wasted costs and workable plans under changed supplies.

title.zh-CN: 同样到岸，为什么会有不同感受？
title.en: Why Can the Same Crossing Feel Different?

summary.zh-CN: 行动与帮助关系、个人/共同/过去参照、故事和计算争用注意；感受是有条件可能性。
summary.en: How do actions, reference points, and attention shape possible feelings?

title.zh-CN: 这条河讲了什么，又省略了什么？
title.en: What Does This River Show, and What Does It Leave Out?

summary.zh-CN: 模型不只省略，还选择因果连接；区分故事留白与执行条件缺失。
summary.en: What does a model connect, and which apparent truths come from its rules?

title.zh-CN: 怎样让朋友照着说明就能开始？
title.en: How Can a Friend Begin from the Instructions?

summary.zh-CN: 围绕一次误读连接一回合一动作、首轮示例、三处纸片、信息显著性与查阅；完整交接留后章。
summary.en: How can wording and components communicate the same executable rules?

title.zh-CN: 帮朋友时，怎样保留她的决定？
title.en: How Can Help Preserve Her Decision?

summary.zh-CN: 从看见、理解、操作、决策逐步分辨支持需要；材料喜好与功能分开；身体表达可有替代。
summary.en: How can assistance make an action possible while preserving its decision?

title.zh-CN: 这一轮，原型要做得多准确？
title.en: How Accurate Does This Prototype Need to Be?

summary.zh-CN: 按本次问题决定哪些规则、材料和呈现要准确，并分清局部演示与整局能回答的事。
summary.en: Choose which rules, materials, and presentation details must be accurate, and distinguish partial checks from whole-game evidence.

title.zh-CN: 请朋友试玩前，要先安排什么？
title.en: What Should You Arrange Before Inviting Friends to Playtest?

summary.zh-CN: 围绕收集来源的问题，安排参与者、版本材料、开场、帮助和停止，以及要留下的事件。
summary.en: Arrange participants, versioned materials, an introduction, help, stopping, and records around a question about collecting.

title.zh-CN: 朋友停下来时，我们究竟知道了什么？
title.en: What Do We Know When a Friend Stops to Ask?

summary.zh-CN: 把一次假想的收集询问逐步拆开，区分事件、玩家解释和主持帮助后能支持的结论。
summary.en: Examine one invented question about collecting and distinguish events, the player’s account, and conclusions after help.

title.zh-CN: 听到几种说法，先查哪件事？
title.en: Several Comments, One Next Question

summary.zh-CN: 把三桌假想试玩的抱怨放回局面，分清可算出的失败、仍未知的原因，以及下一次先查的问题。
summary.en: Put comments from three hypothetical sessions back into their situations, separate known limits from unknown causes, and choose what to investigate next.

title.zh-CN: 下一稿，先改哪里？
title.en: What Should the Next Draft Change First?

summary.zh-CN: 依据假想反馈和当前目标选择 v0.3 材料修订，把可算出的限制与仍需比较的玩法分开。
summary.en: Choose a v0.3 materials revision from hypothetical feedback and current goals, separating calculable limits from changes needing comparison.

title.zh-CN: 你不开口，材料能把一局讲清吗？
title.en: Can the Materials Explain a Game Without You Speaking?

summary.zh-CN: 先提供完整 v0.3 规则和材料，再观察独立准备与运行，并说明帮助会怎样改变结论。
summary.en: Provide complete v0.3 materials and rules before examining independent setup and play, including how help changes conclusions.

title.zh-CN: 别人接手时，怎样拿到同一款游戏？
title.en: How Can Someone Else Receive the Same Game You Intended?

summary.zh-CN: 用完整基本版说明材料交接、版本差异与已查范围，让下一位合作者知道如何继续。
summary.en: Use a complete base version to explain a consistent handoff, changes between versions, and what has actually been checked.

title.zh-CN: 还没读规则，你已经猜到了什么？
title.en: What Have You Already Guessed before Reading the Rules?

summary.zh-CN: 改编选择准备/分派/回程片段；故事熟悉程度不应替另一人决定行动。
summary.en: How should an introduction answer expectations that arrive before the rules?

title.zh-CN: 没动棋子的时候，也在玩吗？
title.en: Are You Still Playing When You Do Not Move a Piece?

summary.zh-CN: 主题吻合的内容仍争用注意；阅读时点与重返局面的支持分开。
summary.en: What can connect a waiting player to a change, and what competes for attention?

title.zh-CN: 不互相攻击，就不会互相影响吗？
title.en: Can We Affect Each Other Without Attacking?

summary.zh-CN: 合法争位与同桌期待分开；允许建议不等于替新手决定。
summary.en: What concrete relationship does a genre label leave unexplained?

title.zh-CN: 先少做一点，和让玩家少选一点
title.en: Making Less and Allowing Fewer Moves Are Different Choices

summary.zh-CN: 用四张节目卡分清缩小制作范围与限制玩家动作，再检查限制是否留下选择和可完成的目标。
summary.en: Use four program cards to separate a smaller production scope from player restrictions, then check choices and completion.

title.zh-CN: 把东西递给朋友以后，他还能怎么选？
title.en: After You Offer Something, What Can Your Friend Choose?

summary.zh-CN: 物品交接的真实后果和拒绝去向；角色、玩家与朋友间评价可能重叠。
summary.en: What makes an offered opportunity meaningful while allowing refusal?

title.zh-CN: 说明书没写的事，也在这一局里发生
title.en: Things the Rulebook Never Wrote Still Happen

summary.zh-CN: 木块可用方式与表达空间如何被组件布置支持；表达留白不让公共数量模糊。
summary.en: How can players add expression without silently changing a shared rule?

title.zh-CN: 加了分数，为什么玩法就变了？
title.en: Why Does Adding a Score Change the Game?

summary.zh-CN: 同分不同参照、进步与落后可同时成立；额外尝试的时间和私人价值。
summary.en: What are people pursuing when we add a score or change its reference?

title.zh-CN: 一个人嫌慢，另一个嫌来不及
title.en: One Friend Says “Too Slow,” Another Says “Too Rushed”

summary.zh-CN: 一个人建议限时，另一个觉得被催时，怎样找到他们各自遇到的困难？
summary.en: When one person wants a timer and another feels rushed, how do we identify their different difficulties?

title.zh-CN: 四个选项，真的比两个更值得想吗？
title.en: Are Four Options More Worth Thinking About Than Two?

summary.zh-CN: 同分卡、七枚石子和六枚石子分别说明选项数量、后果与选择用途。
summary.en: Equal-value cards and seven- and six-stone games distinguish option count, consequences, and the purpose of a choice.

title.zh-CN: 朋友明天才回来，这一回合能留下吗？
title.en: Can a Turn Wait Until Your Friend Comes Back Tomorrow?

summary.zh-CN: 回应之前材料仍可发生在错开时间；撤展日程与个人行动权需要重新协调。
summary.en: What must remain when the person whose turn comes next is absent?

title.zh-CN: 刚才付过了吗？让桌面替人记一件事
title.en: Did We Pay Already? Let the Table Remember Something

summary.zh-CN: 记录要回答丢失的事实；直接计交付片替代总分轨的表示变体与更新代价。
summary.en: Which fact should the table retain after a decision?

title.zh-CN: 平均一样，为什么我还是想选这条路？
title.en: Same Average, So Why Prefer One Route?

summary.zh-CN: 平均都是三盏灯，完成三盏或五盏任务时却可能该选不同路线。
summary.en: Both routes average three lanterns, yet a three- or five-lantern task can favor different routes.

title.zh-CN: 花掉一些水，为什么后来反而更多？
title.en: How Can Spending Water Leave Me With More?

summary.zh-CN: 一笔购买怎样改变后续生产，数量更多又怎样改变损失？
summary.en: Follow how one purchase changes later production and how a larger supply can cause greater losses.
